name: SpaceX

segments.note: The three segments add up to the total operating loss of $2.6B.

footnotes: SpaceX (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.) has not yet filed a 10-K (it listed on Nasdaq on June 12, 2026); figures are the audited FY2025 statements from its Form S-1. They include xAI and X Holdings, retrospectively combined as entities under common control.
Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures (calculated). Debt principal is as of Mar 31, 2026, the latest date in the S-1.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: SpaceX's revenue grew 33.2% to $18.7B in 2025, led by Starlink connectivity, which rose 49.8% to $11.4B as subscribers doubled to 8.9 million. These figures come from its IPO filing (Form S-1) and include xAI and X, which SpaceX combined into its results.

The company swung to a $2.6B operating loss from a $500M profit, because the AI segment lost $6.4B and R&D spending rose 2.5 times to $8.6B. Net loss was $4.9B. Capital spending nearly doubled to $20.7B, so free cash flow was an outflow of about $14.0B.
highlights: Starlink operating income more than doubled to $4.4B, a 38.8% margin.
Starlink subscribers grew to 8.9 million from 4.4 million.
Cash rose to $24.7B after $26.4B of financing inflows.
watch: The AI segment's operating loss widened to $6.4B on $3.2B of revenue.
Starlink average revenue per user fell to $81 a month from $91.
Capital spending of $20.7B was three times operating cash flow; AI took $12.7B of it.
Debt principal reached $29.1B by March 31, 2026, and interest expense was $1.9B in 2025.

revenueLine.say: Starlink connectivity made up 61 percent of revenue and grew 49.8 percent, to 11.4 billion dollars.
